AUTHORED FIGURE BRIEF:
This figure shows two panels, (a) and (b), tracking ten fractional values through a bucket sort. Panel (a) is a vertical column of ten gray cells headed by the italic letter A, with row indices 1 through 10 running down its left side; from top to bottom the cells hold .78, .17, .39, .26, .72, .94, .21, .12, .23, and .68. Panel (b) is a second vertical column of ten gray cells headed B and indexed 0 through 9, each cell serving as the head of a linked list. The cells at indices 0, 4, 5, and 8 contain only a diagonal slash. The rest carry a horizontal arrow into a chain of two-field records, each record showing a value on the left and either a pointer arrow or a terminating slash on the right: index 1 leads to .12 then .17, index 2 to .21, .23, then .26, index 3 to .39 alone, index 6 to .68, index 7 to .72 then .78, and index 9 to .94. Each chain is in increasing order, and the leading digit of every value matches the index of the cell whose chain holds it, which is the correspondence the two columns invite the reader to check. The panels walk through distributing numbers drawn from the half-open interval from 0 to 1 into equal-width buckets, after which concatenating the sorted lists in index order gives the sorted output.

REQUESTED INTERACTIONS:
- Code editor for bucket sort distribution: learner writes bucketIndex(x) = floor(10*x) and insertSorted(bucket, x); running the code sends each value from A into the correct B[i] linked list and preserves sorted order inside nonempty buckets.
- Step through the input array: each press processes the next A cell, highlights the computed interval [i/10, (i+1)/10), and draws the new node in the selected bucket.
- Boundary-case tests: learner tries values near 0 and 1, and the diagram flags the half-open bucket convention that keeps .94 in bucket 9 while values like .12 and .17 land in bucket 1.

SOURCE FILE: Introduction to Algorithms, Figure 8.4

There is no blueprint: decide the figure type, elements, labels, controls, and any step sequence yourself.
